content.comment_body: Hello, I've noticed that my UDFs tend to become corrupted rather easily. The specific error message is shown in the attached files. Here's what happens: I create a UDF using [product_name], save it, and it works well when inserted into a program. I can upload the program to my device as well. However, after some time (a few days), when I edit the program again, the UDF is corrupted and can't be opened. This has occurred twice. Each time, I recreated the UDF from scratch, using the same name. Checking the UDF's XML in a text editor shows it looks fine. If needed, I can upload it for review. I'm using Windows 7 64-bit with [product_name] [version_no]. Does anyone have suggestions or ideas on how to keep this from happening?
A user on the German forum described a similar issue. Their situation involved nested UDFs (UDF within a UDF). They faced the same problem but did not investigate further. [url]

Strange situation. I deleted the UDF file and opened the main program. The UDF block showed a red indicator. When I right-clicked and selected 'Expand UDF,' it opened the UDF in the editor as a new unsaved instance, and I was able to save it. This suggests that the UDF is also stored within the main project file. Something unusual happened, because previously I couldn't open it via 'Expand UDF' nor directly using the standard Open menu. I'm still interested to learn what caused this, but a solution may not appear soon. I'll share updates if I discover more. I attached a screenshot of the UDF so you can see it's quite simple. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users have observed that UDF (User Defined Function) files created in [product_name] may become corrupted after several days, even if the files appear normal when inspected in a text editor and initially function correctly. The issue seems inconsistent, leading to uncertainty and occasional data loss. Sometimes, utilizing the 'Expand UDF' feature within the software can serve as a workaround, implying that UDFs might be stored redundantly in both project and UDF files.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect UDF files to remain accessible and functional after saving, without unexpected corruption. Additionally, they hope for clear error messages and ways to prevent such issues in future versions.
